slides.h: Rugs: splurge on //size//, skip the label.
slides.dek: The most common money mistake in the living room is sixty centimetres too small.

slides.h: A floating rug shrinks the room.
body: A rug that stops at the coffee table turns the seating into an island and the floor into a corridor.
It reads temporary, whatever it cost.
Front legs of every seat on the rug, with margin to spare. The rug should define the zone, not decorate the middle of it.
Size is visible from the doorway. Nothing else about a rug is.
An oversized flatweave in plain wool outranks a small signature piece at the same price.
Pattern and provenance disappear under a coffee table. The extra metre never does.

slides.h: Measure the seating zone, then round up.
body: Tape the rectangle your sofa and chairs sit in, add thirty centimetres each side, and buy that.
When two sizes bracket the number, the larger one is the answer.

slides.h: Save this before the rug order.
